clue.text: Chop stick? Start to chop up sticks

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of chop is taken

parts.note: to up sticks is a British idiom for moving house, i.e. to leave

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at chopsticks, then advice to begin chopping up some sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop stick?' reads as chopsticks, but it asks for one word meaning both chop and stick. 'Start to' takes C from 'chop'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two opposite senses, to split apart and to adhere, so it means both chop and stick.

clue.text: Top river, topping one with fish

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece on top comes first, so the river is placed above the rest

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
I is the Roman numeral one
the sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A recipe of sorts: river fish served with a topping.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless top worn by women, a garment covering the upper body.

clue.text: Legal right of European people in Orient

indicators.note: the European and the people are placed inside the word for the Orient

parts.note: the Orient is the East
people, as in a group of workers or soldiers, are men

explanation.surface: Asks about the legal rights of Europeans living in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: An easement is a legal entitlement to use another's land, such as a right of way.

clue.text: Beehive State's boxing match

indicators.note: the words box up the answer, holding it inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: Points to a boxing bout in Utah, nicknamed the Beehive State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing match' looks like a sporting event; 'boxing' is the indicator and 'match' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vesta is an old name for a short wooden or wax friction match, named after the Roman hearth goddess.

clue.text: Works of art and more of the same — items needing no introduction

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and more of the same

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: items are things

explanation.surface: A list of artworks and similar pieces so famous they need no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints made from engraved metal plates, a classic kind of artwork.

clue.text: Enter with pair of boots, posing dramatic question

indicators.note: posing suggests striking a new attitude, so the letters are set in a new arrangement
a pair means two, so the word is taken twice

parts.note: one of the boots is a boot

explanation.surface: A stage direction: an actor comes on wearing boots and strikes a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' doubles BOOT; with ENTER that gives the thirteen letters that 'posing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's famous soliloquy opens with this question about whether to go on living, the best-known question in drama.

clue.text: Pantomime character, one of five, after last bit of water in well

indicators.note: the quintuplet comes after the rest
the final letter of water is set inside the word for well

parts.note: hale means healthy, or well

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: A pantomime figure appears after the water in a well runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a noun, a water source, but it is the adjective meaning healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the masked clown of the harlequinade, a stock figure in traditional pantomime.

clue.text: Turned on with repeated gentle reproach

indicators.note: repeated means the two-part piece appears twice running
turned round, the little word on is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone switched on and kept being mildly told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' looks like a phrase meaning excited; 'Turned' reverses ON to NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Said twice in a soothing tone, the phrase is a mild rebuke, like 'come, come'.

clue.text: Cricket club almost heading for disaster is found out

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: Sussex is an English county cricket club

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricket club close to calamity has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: SUSSEX is an English county with a first-class cricket side; 'almost' cuts it to SUSSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussed is British slang for worked out or discovered, matching found out.

clue.text: Grandma who supposes erroneously

definitions.meaning: Grandma ... was the celebrated American folk painter who began painting in old age
from the tongue-twister song in Singin' in the Rain, where this man supposes his toeses are roses, erroneously

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a person: the folk artist known by her nickname and the figure in the patter song lyric.

clue.text: Passengers initially go swimmingly in bus designed for local tours

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken
the swimming stroke is put inside the rearranged bus
designed suggests something worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to crawl is to swim using the front crawl stroke

explanation.surface: A bus specially built for passengers to cruise round the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the bus to UBS before the stroke goes in. 'local' is British slang for a nearby pub, so the definition is a tour of locals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is a tour of several pubs, and a local is a neighbourhood pub, so these are local tours.

clue.text: Prince Philip supporting soldier or old sailor

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
Prince Philip was the husband, so the man, of the Queen, ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: Asks whether Prince Philip backed a soldier or an old sea dog.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; Prince Philip was her man.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateersman was a sailor on a privateer, a privately owned ship licensed to attack enemy shipping in former times.

clue.text: Congenial postman introduces himself, entering like this with circular letter

indicators.note: the postman's self-introduction goes into the Latin word for thus

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, like this
Postman Pat, the British children's TV character, would say I'm Pat
O is the round letter

explanation.surface: A friendly postman introduces himself while delivering a circular.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV series about a village postman. 'circular letter' looks like a junk mailshot; it is just O.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico, borrowed from Italian and Spanish, means likeable and easy to get along with.

clue.text: Call up first mate to cover green light

indicators.note: the first piece wraps around the second, covering it

parts.note: Eve was Adam's mate, the first woman
a green light is approval, an OK

explanation.surface: A ship's first mate must arrange cover for the green navigation light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first mate' suggests a ship's officer; it is Eve, the first wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon up a memory or feeling, to call it to mind.

clue.text: Running round town, lag in marathon

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move, so they are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A slow runner trails round the town during a marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marathon' looks like the race, but used as an adjective it means interminably long.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon session is one that goes on and on, drawn out far longer than expected.

clue.text: Security devices needed as a dodo flies?

parts.note: the saying is dead as a dodo
to fly off is to bolt, so flies means bolts

explanation.surface: Wonders what is needed when a dodo takes flight, which it never could.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like the insects or a bird flying; it means rushes away, bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadbolts are locks with a bolt moved by key rather than spring, used to secure doors.

clue.text: Unfold chart showing office organisation

parts.note: to unfold something is to open it
a chart or diagram is a plan

explanation.surface: Instructions to unfold a chart that maps out an office.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office has no internal walls, a way of laying out a workplace.

clue.text: Doctor's replacement, quiet life preserver in London area

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the alter ego who replaces Dr Jekyll
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
Noah's ark preserved life through the flood

explanation.surface: A doctor's locum keeps a quiet lifebelt somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life preserver' suggests a lifebelt; it is Noah's ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London.

clue.text: Come along and play with elastic band?

definitions.meaning: pulling and releasing a rubber band makes it give a sharp crack

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an order to be quick, and taken literally describes making something give a snap.

clue.text: Posh policeman defending article that's put online?

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: the policeman surrounds the article, guarding it

parts.note: plod is British slang for a police officer, after Mr Plod in Noddy
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An upper-class officer protects a piece of writing that has been published on the web.
explanation.definitionFit: To upload is to transfer a file to the internet or a server.

clue.text: Leg trapped by girl lying down

indicators.note: the leg is caught inside the girl's name

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
pins is slang for legs, so a leg is a pin

explanation.surface: A girl has her leg caught while she is lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on one's back, face upward.

clue.text: Tree said to be sound

indicators.note: said signals that the word for the tree is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree

explanation.surface: A tree is reported to be in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy; it is the verb, to measure depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb a sea is to sound it, measuring its depth with a weighted line.

clue.text: Old family member taking trip over border

indicators.note: the trip takes in the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a trip or outing is a ride
gran is a grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly relative goes on a journey across a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' looks like a frontier crossed; the river itself is the US-Mexico border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande forms much of the boundary between the United States and Mexico.

clue.text: Lightning attack seizing power

indicators.note: the attack grabs the power and holds it inside

parts.note: a raid is an attack
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A lightning attack captures control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightning attack' reads as a blitz; 'Lightning' alone is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightning, used as an adjective, means very fast.

clue.text: Flag email from criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flag message sent by a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red banner of the abbey of St Denis, carried by French kings into battle.

clue.text: Dance music and pop entertaining uninitiated people

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the father holds the other piece inside

parts.note: pop is a name for father, pa

indicators.note: uninitiated means without the first letter

parts.note: folk are people

explanation.surface: Dance music and pop played to entertain newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like the music genre beside 'Dance music'; it is Dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A polka is a lively Bohemian dance and the music written for it.

clue.text: Sauce covering one's birthday suit

definitions.meaning: a liquid seasoning, as for a salad
the birthday suit is bare skin, so covering it is putting clothes on

explanation.definitionFit: Salad seasoning such as vinaigrette is called this, and so is the act of putting clothes on.

clue.text: Desperate guy's entering Greek port

indicators.note: the guy's name goes inside the abbreviation for Greek

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman cowboy of the British comic the Dandy

explanation.surface: A desperate man arrives in a Greek harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a character in the British comic the Dandy. 'Greek port' looks like one phrase; Gdansk is Polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a major Baltic seaport in northern Poland.
